text_version.note: Trimmed 2026-10-14 to the bill's AI-Act implementation part: article 24 (titre V bis LCEN) and articles 24 bis to 24 terdecies added by the Senate. Articles 24 decies (CPCE/ARCEP-type agents), 24 undecies (code monétaire et financier, ACPR), 24 duodecies (loi Informatique et libertés, CNIL) and 24 terdecies (loi 1986, Arcom) also implement Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and were kept, beyond the requested 24 bis-24 nonies range. Article 63 (code du travail, labour-inspection market surveillance) also cites Regulation 2024/1689 in passing but is not included. The existing annotation (annotations/<id>.json) was made on the untrimmed text: only 48 of its 343 quotes occur in the trimmed text (most lost quotes come from non-AI articles).

summary.short: Article 24 of a French bill adapting national law to the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) makes AI systems subject to the regulation, designates national market-surveillance and notifying authorities across sectors, and sets their investigation, injunction and administrative-fine powers. Pending Senate-adopted text.
summary.long: Article 24 of a French bill adapting national law to the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) sets out how the regulation is applied and enforced nationally. The Senate-adopted text, pending in the Assemblée nationale, inserts a Title V bis into the 2004 digital economy law (Art. 55-1 to 55-6): AI systems are subject to the regulation, authorities may share information, agents may inspect and fine notified bodies in the toy sector, and fines follow the regulation's Art. 99 ceilings. Art. 24 bis authorises an ordinance, within six months of promulgation, on overseas adaptation and regulatory sandboxes. Art. 24 ter gives the Conseil d'État, Cour de cassation and Cour des comptes oversight of high-risk AI used in judicial functions. Further articles amend the environment, consumer, construction, defence, transport, public health, postal and electronic communications, monetary and financial, data protection (1978) and audiovisual (1986) laws, assigning market-surveillance, notification, certification and fine powers to the CNIL, Arcom, the health agency, the consumer authority, the transport minister, the radio-frequency agency and the financial supervisor. Authorities may order injunctions, suspension, withdrawal, recall and fines. The excerpt gives no entry-into-force date for Article 24.

notes: Excerpt of the Senate-adopted bill (first reading, registered at the Assemblée nationale 20 Feb 2026), covering Titre IV Art. 24 to 24 terdecies only; other provisions are elided with […], so text_version.extent is partial. The AI Act is cited as règlement (UE) 2024/1689, which is not in the registry, so target ids are null. Placeholders read loi n° du portant diverses dispositions (Art. 24 nonies 13 b and 15 b; Art. 24 undecies 5 a); the bill's title as given in Art. 24 nonies 13 b omits d’information and agriculture et de pêche, which the cover title includes. Cross-references to 2022-582 and 2022-1086 ordinances (medical devices) are not coded as relations.
